mentalMap.label: Data structures
mentalMap.sub: linked list of blocks + Merkle tree inside → two levels of hashing, one level of linking

mentalMap.label: Merkle trees
mentalMap.sub: pair up → hash up → root in header; proof = one sibling hash per level

mentalMap.label: Shared data
mentalMap.sub: public on-chain / permissioned on-chain / private off-chain + hash anchor

mentalMap.label: Protocols
mentalMap.sub: application (what) → consensus (which order) → gossip (how it travels)

mentalMap.label: Fat protocols
mentalMap.sub: thin carries messages, fat carries rules + state; smart contracts are the hinge

mentalMap.label: Platforms
mentalMap.sub: who may write / how they agree / when it is final

mentalMap.label: DApps
mentalMap.sub: front end, wallet, node, contract, oracle — the wallet must not belong to the operator

mentalMap.label: Smart contracts
mentalMap.sub: deploy → address → call → gas-metered execute → event; code frozen, state moves

topExamQuestions: Explain the main data structures of a blockchain and why a linked list of hashes beats a flat table. (5 marks)
Build a Merkle tree level by level and prove inclusion of one transaction using sibling hashes, with the number of hash nodes per level and the proof length. (15 marks)
Distinguish public, permissioned and private shared data and explain how private data keeps tamper-evidence. (5 marks)
Explain the three protocol layers in a blockchain and what each is responsible for. (5 marks)
Distinguish thin and fat protocols and explain why smart contracts make a protocol fat. (5 marks)
Compare Ethereum, Hyperledger Fabric, Corda and Quorum by identity model, consensus and finality. (5 marks)
Describe the anatomy of a decentralised application and how each part maps onto a business model. (5 marks)
Explain deploy-and-execute semantics of smart contracts, immutable code versus mutable state, gas, events and access control. (15 marks)
drill: What links blocks and what links transactions?
The previous block hash links blocks; the Merkle root links the transactions inside a block.
Why not a flat table?
A row can be edited in place with no visible consequence; the hash chain turns any edit into a cascade of mismatches to the tip.
How many internal nodes for n leaves?
n-1. Four leaves → 3 internal nodes.
How many hashing levels for 1,024 leaves?
What is in a Merkle proof for leaf A of a 4-leaf tree?
H(B) and H(C|D) — the sibling hash at each level, nothing else.
Where does the Merkle root live?
In the block header.
Where does private data live?
Off-chain; only its hash is anchored on-chain.
Name the three protocol layers.
Application, consensus, gossip — over TCP/IP.
Thin vs fat: where do the rules live?
Thin: in the application. Fat: in the protocol, inside contracts.
What makes a protocol fat?
Smart contracts putting rules and state into the protocol.
What are the three platform questions?
Who may write, how nodes agree, when finality arrives.
Corda's model?
Permissioned with a notary model for bilateral contracts.
Name the five dApp parts.
Front end, wallet, node/provider, smart contract, oracle.
Which dApp part must the operator not control?
The wallet — the user signs with their own key, so no custody.
Immutable vs mutable in a contract?
The deployed code is immutable; the state it manages is mutable.
What does a revert do to gas?
Burns the gas used; only the unused remainder is refunded.
Cost of a plain ETH transfer?
21,000 gas — about 0.00042 ETH at 20 gwei, ~1,400 per 30M-gas block.
Why do events exist?
So apps follow state changes from logs without reading the whole ledger.
Where is access control enforced?
In the contract's own code — owner and role checks, usually modifiers.
